title: Florida House, District 72
what_it_does: Represents District 72 (Part of Manatee) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings.

candidates.name: William Conerly
candidates.occupation: Civil engineer; owner and vice president at Kimley-Horn and Associates; state representative for District 72 since 2024
candidates.background: Fifth-generation Floridian and Lakewood Ranch resident who served nearly six years in the U.S. Navy and holds an engineering degree. He is an owner and vice president at Kimley-Horn and Associates. He was elected to the House in 2024.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted yes on HJR 1-F in the June 2026 special session, which placed Amendment 3 on the November ballot to raise the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and to limit how counties and cities may spend property-tax revenue. His website says he voted to eliminate property taxes.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HJR 1F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), passage 75-26
Bill Conerly for State Representative (campaign website)

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (2025), which created the State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state help with federal detainers, barred driver licenses for unauthorized immigrants, and funded an Unauthorized Alien Transport Program. His website says he expanded E-Verify to all Florida employers and supported local law enforcement enforcing immigration laws.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), passage 85-30
Bill Conerly for State Representative (campaign website)

taxes.summary: His website says he cut billions in state taxes and made sales-tax holidays permanent.

sources.title: Bill Conerly for State Representative (campaign website)

trump.summary: His website says he is running to take quick action, just like President Trump.
trump.quote: I am running to take quick action, just like President Trump.

sources.title: Bill Conerly for State Representative (campaign website)

other_issues.title: Property insurance
other_issues.summary: He pledges to lower insurance rates 'come hell or highwater' and says he passed laws to lower rates; no specific mechanism stated.

sources.title: Bill Conerly for State Representative (campaign website)

other_issues.title: Environment
other_issues.summary: His website lists protecting state parks from development, blocking offshore drilling and eliminating PFAS pollutants among his accomplishments.

sources.title: Bill Conerly for State Representative (campaign website)

record.item: Voted yes on CS/HJR 1F (homestead property-tax exemption increase / Amendment 3), House passage 75-26, June 2, 2026.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HJR 1F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), passage 75-26

record.item: Voted yes on SB 2-C (Immigration enforcement), House passage 85-30, Feb. 13, 2025.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), passage 85-30

record.item: Voted for CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; because the vote sent the question to voters rather than cutting taxes itself, a vote for it is coded as leaning toward sharply reducing homestead property taxes rather than as full agreement.

sources.title: Bill page
Roll-call vote

record.item: Voted for SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.

sources.title: Bill page
Roll-call vote

candidates.name: Harvey Shifrin
candidates.occupation: Attorney and certified public accountant; substitute teacher and adjunct law professor
candidates.background: Attorney and certified public accountant with decades of experience in law and finance who has worked with students for 27 years through Odyssey of the Mind and Destination Imagination, served as a substitute teacher and taught as an adjunct professor at John Marshall School of Law.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

abortion.summary: He said government has limited interest in restricting abortion before viability and called the six-week ban unreasonable. He also said he would work to decriminalize physicians providing medical treatment.
abortion.quote: I believe that Florida's six-week ban is unreasonable and cruel.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 72 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

property_tax.summary: He opposes Amendment 3, the 2026 measure raising the homestead exemption, saying it limits county spending. He favors shifting the tax burden toward higher-end and investor-owned housing.
property_tax.quote: The current Proposition 3, while reducing taxes by increasing the homestead exemption, is really a poison apple, disguising limitations on counties to spend tax dollars

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 72 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

education_choice.summary: He calls the voucher program disastrous and says he would reform it, improve teacher pay and strengthen public schools. His website calls for "fair funding by reforming the voucher system."
education_choice.quote: I would also work to improve teacher pay (Florida now ranks 50th) and to reform the disastrous voucher program.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 72 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)
Harvey Shifrin for Florida House District 72, campaign website (accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

growth.summary: He would work to reverse recent state laws limiting local control over development, naming SB 180 and SB 1520, and to restore home rule. He says he is not against development but wants it planned around infrastructure.
growth.quote: I am not anti-development, but I believe all development must exist withing a framework of appropriate planning and infrastructure.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 72 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)
Harvey Shifrin for Florida House District 72, campaign website (accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

healthcare.summary: He said the state should stop limiting Medicaid availability and invest more in health care, including Medicaid.
healthcare.quote: Florida has been working to limit availability of Medicaid. I believe this should stop. We should be investing more into our healthcare system, including Medicaid availability.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 72 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

immigration.summary: Discussing housing costs, he said a "national draconian approach to immigration" has made construction workers scarce. He did not lay out a broader immigration position.
immigration.quote: Combined with the national draconian approach to immigration, construction workers are scarce, further driving up both the price and the pace of construction.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 72 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)
